threads.thread_goal: Align on overall hybrid course structure and weekly plan.

messages.text: Morning all, sharing a first pass at the hybrid weekly structure for the first-year course, based on T1 and the draft in A1 for project_title: Hybrid First-Year Teaching Redesign with Virtual Learning Environments. Weeks 1–4: blended intro and core concepts, with one on-site slot and one online slot per week. Weeks 5–8: more lab-heavy, with on-site focus and online prep/debrief. Weeks 9–12: project and consolidation, mostly online with targeted on-site support. Learning outcomes are mapped week by week in A1 so they align with the programme outcomes. For the first four weeks I have: Week 1: orientation, expectations, basic concepts (online orientation + on-site icebreaker and diagnostic). Week 2: core theory block 1 (online content + on-site workshop). Week 3: core theory block 2 (online content + on-site problem-solving). Week 4: intro to lab/practical (online safety + on-site demo). Can you review whether this balance works, and flag anything that might clash with existing lab capacity or support needs before we lock in D1 and D2?

Thanks for pulling this together. Looking at A1, I like that each week has a clear outcome. One question: for Week 1, could we make the on-site diagnostic more structured so we can spot students with learning difficulties early, not just content gaps? Maybe a short reflective task plus a quick checklist we can later connect to the support plan in T5. Also, for Week 3, do we have enough time in the on-site problem-solving slot to include group work, or should some of that move to the online component?

Good points. On Week 1, I suggest we add a short online self-check activity before the on-site diagnostic, so we can use the on-site time to follow up with anyone who flags concerns. That can sit in the orientation piece that will later link to T9. For Week 3, we can split: online pre-work with individual problems, then use the on-site slot for small-group application and a quick wrap-up. That keeps the timetable intact and should still hit the learning outcomes listed in A1.

From a classroom management angle, I like that each week has one clear on-site focus. For Weeks 2 and 3, could we be explicit in A1 about which activities are synchronous online versus self-paced? I want to avoid students assuming everything online is optional. Maybe we mark one live online slot in Week 2 for Q and A, and keep Week 3 fully asynchronous online so they can work around other modules.

I am just checking: for Week 4, when we say online safety, is that a video plus quiz, or a live session? I am thinking about the lab rules and whether we need them to sign something before they come on-site. Also, do we already have the lab timetable confirmed, or should we wait before we finalise Week 4 in A1?

For Week 4, my proposal is: pre-recorded safety video plus a short online quiz they must pass before attending the on-site demo. We can also add a simple acknowledgement form in the VLE. That fits with T6 and the lab procedures in A5 we will finalise later. Lab timetable is confirmed for the existing slot, so we can safely keep the on-site demo there. I will update A1 to make that explicit.

On the split between online and on-site for the first four weeks, here is a concrete proposal so we can move toward D2: Week 1: online orientation and self-check; on-site diagnostic and community-building. Week 2: online content plus one live online Q and A; on-site workshop. Week 3: online fully asynchronous problem set; on-site group problem-solving. Week 4: online safety video and quiz; on-site lab demo. This keeps synchronous time within the existing timetable and uses online for prep and consolidation.

I am happy with that split for D2. It is clear enough to explain to students, and we can mirror it in the orientation materials later. Only small ask: in Week 2, can we keep the live online Q and A to 30 minutes max so it does not clash with other modules informal sessions?

Agree with the Week 1–4 structure as you outlined. From a support perspective, I will make sure the Week 1 diagnostic includes a short reflection prompt about previous learning experiences, so we can spot who might need extra help. That will feed into T5 and T11 later. No concerns from me on D2.

I am ok with that plan too. I just want to check how we will explain to students which sessions are compulsory. Maybe we can mark them clearly in A1 and then copy that wording into the VLE later, so they do not miss the on-site diagnostic or the lab demo.

Good call. I will mark compulsory sessions explicitly in A1 and later in the VLE structure when we work on T4. Before we close D1, can you all confirm you are comfortable with the overall weekly flow across the semester as drafted in A1, not just Weeks 1–4? In particular, the shift to more project work in Weeks 9–12.

I have gone through the rest of A1. The progression from core concepts to labs to project work looks coherent, and the learning outcomes per week line up with what we already tell students in the programme handbook. I do not see any clashes with school holidays or known assessment peaks in other first-year modules.

Same here, I checked A1 against the programme outcomes and it looks aligned. The only thing I will watch is that we keep some recap time in Weeks 10–11 for students who struggle with pace, but that is more about how we design activities than the outline itself. I am fine to approve the weekly structure as it stands.

I do not have any objections. The lab-heavy weeks match when the lab is usually quieter, so that should be manageable. I will just need clear instructions later from T6 on how to run the hybrid labs, but that can come after we lock the outline.

I have cross-checked the outline in A1 with the existing assessment map draft in A2, and the timing still works once we refine T2. No red flags from me. I am comfortable confirming the overall weekly structure and learning outcomes as our baseline.

Thanks all. Summarising so we can close this out: 1) Weeks 1–4 will follow the online versus on-site split that 492230 outlined in M7, including the Week 4 safety video and quiz before the lab demo. 2) Across the semester, we keep the progression in A1: early blended foundation, mid-semester lab focus, end-of-semester project and consolidation. 3) We will mark compulsory sessions clearly in A1 and later in the VLE when we work on T4. With that, I propose we treat the current version of A1 as approved for D1, with any further tweaks being minor wording changes rather than structural shifts.

Happy with that summary and with treating A1 as our baseline. Once you update the compulsory session labels, can you drop a quick note here so we know it is ready to share with the programme coordinator?
Will do. I will update A1 today with the compulsory session labels and the clarified Week 1–4 split, then share it with the programme coordinator as part of T1.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize assessment plan, rubrics, and feedback approach.

messages.text: Picking up the assessment side: I have uploaded a draft assessment map and initial rubrics into A2 for project_title: Hybrid First-Year Teaching Redesign with Virtual Learning Environments, linked to T2. Headline proposal: Assessment 1: low-stakes online quiz in Week 2 (5 percent) to check core concepts. Assessment 2: lab skills check in Week 6 (20 percent), with a simple rubric. Assessment 3: midterm applied assignment in Week 8 (25 percent). Assessment 4: final project with presentation in Week 12 (40 percent). Plus 10 percent for ongoing participation, tracked via VLE and on-site attendance. Rubrics are sketched for Assessments 2–4. Can you review the weightings and timing, and flag any clashes with other modules before we confirm D3?

I like the spread overall. One concern: 40 percent on the final project might be heavy for first-years, especially those still adjusting to hybrid study. Could we shift 5 percent from the final project to the midterm applied assignment, so they have a bit more incentive to engage earlier? That would make the midterm 30 percent and the final 35 percent, still keeping the total at 100.

From a support angle, I agree with spreading the weight a bit more. Also, for the lab skills check in Week 6, could we make sure the rubric in A2 includes a criterion for safe practice, not just technical accuracy? That will tie in nicely with the lab guidelines in A5 and T6.

I am looking at the participation 10 percent. How exactly are we planning to measure that? Is it just attendance, or also online activity? I want to be sure I record it correctly in the VLE and do not miss anything that should go into A8 later.

Good question. My suggestion: participation 10 percent is a mix of attendance and engagement. For now, we can define it as: 5 percent for consistent attendance (on-site and online live sessions) and 5 percent for completion of key online activities (quizzes, discussion posts). We can capture that in A8 and T8 when we finalise the tracking process. It will need clear guidance in A6 so we are consistent.

I am comfortable with that adjustment. New proposal for D3: Assessment 1 quiz 5 percent, Assessment 2 lab skills 20 percent, Assessment 3 midterm applied assignment 30 percent, Assessment 4 final project 35 percent, Participation 10 percent. This keeps the total at 100 and shifts a bit more weight earlier. I will update A2 accordingly if everyone agrees.
That breakdown works for me. It should also help with motivation in the middle of the semester. No clashes that I can see with other first-year assessments, based on the latest programme calendar.

I support that distribution too. For students who struggle, having more weight on the midterm gives us a chance to intervene earlier if they underperform, especially if we connect it to the check-ins in T11.
I am ok with the new percentages. For the participation part, once we have the template in A8, I will probably need an example filled in so I can follow it correctly.

Great, I will treat that as agreed for D3 and update A2 today. On rubrics: I have drafted analytic rubrics for the lab skills check, midterm, and final project in A2. They all use four bands (excellent, good, developing, limited) with descriptors. We now need to align our feedback approach and the comment bank in T10 with these rubrics and the norms in A6 so students get consistent messages.

On feedback, I suggest we standardise around three elements for each major assessment: 1) one or two specific strengths linked to rubric criteria, 2) one or two specific areas to improve, again tied to the rubric, and 3) a short forward-looking suggestion. We can capture this in A6 and build the comment bank in T10 around those patterns. That should help us keep tone constructive and avoid vague comments.

I like that structure. Could we also agree on a rough word range for written feedback, so students in different groups do not compare and feel they got less attention? For example, 80–120 words for the lab skills check, 150–200 for the midterm and final project. We can note that in A6.

Can we also build in some inclusive language examples into the comment bank in T10? For instance, avoiding labels about the student and focusing on the work, and offering options for how they might approach tasks differently next time. That will help students with learning difficulties feel supported rather than judged.

I sometimes struggle to phrase feedback quickly. Will the comment bank in T10 include ready-made phrases we can adapt, or just guidelines? Having some concrete examples in A6 would really help me stay consistent.

The plan for T10 is to include both: a set of ready-to-use comments aligned with each rubric criterion in A2, plus short guidance in A6 on how to personalise them. We can also add a few do and do not examples for tone and clarity.

On turnaround times, I propose we document in A6 that: quizzes and low-stakes tasks get feedback within 3 days (mostly automated), lab skills and midterm within 10 working days, and final project within 15 working days. That should be realistic with our teaching loads and still helpful for students.

Those turnaround times work for me. If we stick to them, students should get feedback in time to use it on the next task. I suggest we also add in A6 that we will use the same basic structure for feedback across all groups, as you outlined earlier.

Agreed. I will pay particular attention to the midterm feedback, since that is where we can signpost students to extra support if needed. As long as we all use the same structure and comment bank from T10, students should get a consistent experience.
I am ok with those timelines. I might need a reminder at busy points, but having them written in A6 will help me plan.

To wrap this up: 1) We have agreed the assessment types, weightings, and deadlines as per M24, and I will lock those into A2 and share with the programme coordinator for formal sign-off under T2. 2) For feedback, we will use the shared structure (strengths, areas to improve, forward-looking suggestion), common word ranges, and agreed turnaround times, all documented in A6. 3) T10 will deliver a comment bank with inclusive, rubric-linked examples that we all use. With that, I think we can record D4 as agreed on the shared feedback standards and comment bank, alongside D3 on the assessment plan.

threads.thread_goal: Define inclusion strategies and support for learning difficulties.

messages.text: I have drafted an inclusion and learning difficulties support plan in A3, linked to T5, for project_title: Hybrid First-Year Teaching Redesign with Virtual Learning Environments. It covers: 1) proactive adjustments in teaching (clear structure, chunked content, multiple formats), 2) assessment adjustments (extra time, alternative formats where approved), 3) communication practices (plain language, consistent reminders), and 4) early check-ins and referral routes, which connect to T11. Could you review and suggest which practices we want to make core for all groups so we can confirm D5?

Thanks for pulling this together. For core practices, I would definitely include: clear weekly checklists in the VLE, predictable deadlines, and using the same structure for each online module. Those help all students, not just those with identified difficulties. I also like the idea of short recap videos for key concepts, but we might need to be realistic about how many we can produce before semester start.

I agree on the universal design elements. For D5, I suggest we treat the following as non-negotiable across all groups: 1) consistent weekly structure in the VLE, 2) clear signposting of what is compulsory versus optional, 3) multiple ways to engage with core content (at least slides plus one other format), and 4) early check-ins in Weeks 2 and 4 as described in T11. More specialised adjustments can then be handled case by case with the student support officer.

I am reading A3 now. For the early check-ins, do we have a template for what to ask students, or do we just talk to them informally? I want to be sure I do not miss important questions, especially for those who might not speak up easily.

Good point. We can build a simple check-in template as part of T11: a short online form plus a few guiding questions for in-class conversations. A3 can reference that so we are all asking similar things about workload, understanding, and any barriers to participation.

On recap videos, I agree we need to be realistic. How about we commit to short audio or video summaries only for the most concept-heavy weeks (probably Weeks 2, 3, and 7), and for other weeks we rely on clear written summaries and structured slides? I can update A3 to reflect that as a recommended, not mandatory, practice.
That sounds manageable. If we focus the audio or video summaries on the trickiest topics, we will get most of the benefit without overloading ourselves.

One more thing for D5: I think we should explicitly include in A3 that we will use plain language in instructions and avoid last-minute changes to deadlines unless absolutely necessary. When changes are unavoidable, we should communicate them in at least two channels (VLE announcement and in-class reminder). That predictability is crucial for students who rely on routines.

I can do that. It helps me too to have things planned. Will A3 also include examples of how to phrase instructions more clearly? Sometimes I write long paragraphs and I am not sure if students follow.
Yes, I can add a short section in A3 with before and after examples of instructions, showing how to break them into steps and use bullet points. That should help all of us keep things clearer.

On assessment adjustments, I assume we will still follow institutional processes for formal accommodations, and not make ad hoc changes on our own. Maybe A3 can remind us to check with the student support officer before agreeing to anything beyond what is already approved.

Agreed. We should not commit to adjustments that go beyond policy without checking. A3 can state that any formal changes to assessment conditions must be confirmed with the student support officer or programme coordinator, and we stick to the standard options otherwise.

To make D5 concrete, here is a proposed list of core practices we all commit to: 1) Consistent weekly VLE structure with checklists and clear labels for compulsory versus optional activities. 2) Multiple formats for core content where feasible (slides plus at least one other format). 3) Plain language instructions and advance notice of any changes, communicated in at least two channels. 4) Early check-ins in Weeks 2 and 4 using a shared template from T11, with a clear route to refer students to support. 5) Respecting institutional processes for formal assessment adjustments, with no ad hoc promises. Everything else in A3 is recommended but flexible. Are we all comfortable with that as our shared baseline?
Yes, that list works for me. It is clear enough to follow and still leaves room for individual teaching styles.
I am ok with that too. Having the checklist in the VLE will help me remember what to post each week.

I am happy with that baseline. I will update A3 to highlight these as core practices and mark the rest as recommended. Once that is done, I will share it with the student support officer for a quick review as part of T5 and T11.

Great. Let us record D5 as: we will apply the five core inclusion and support practices listed in M51 across all groups, as documented in A3, and use T11 to operationalise the early check-ins and referral process.

threads.thread_goal: Lock down VLE configuration, orientation module, and tracking processes.

messages.text: Quick update on the VLE side for project_title: Hybrid First-Year Teaching Redesign with Virtual Learning Environments. I have set up the basic course shell using the checklist in A4 and linked it to T4: weekly modules for Weeks 1–12, placeholders for content, and a draft gradebook that matches the assessment plan in A2. Attendance and announcements tools are enabled but not fully configured yet. For T9, I have also started a student orientation module following the outline in A7. Before we sign off D6 and D7, we need to agree on: 1) final navigation structure (what appears in the main menu), 2) how we present the orientation module, and 3) the exact process for attendance and participation tracking in T8 using A8.

Thanks for the update. On navigation, I would keep the main menu as simple as possible: Home, Weekly modules, Assessments, Labs, Support, and Announcements. Anything else can sit inside those sections. That should help first-years find things quickly.

For the Support section, could we include a clear link to the inclusion guide summary from A3 and information about how to contact the student support officer? That will connect the VLE structure to the support plan in T5 and T11.

I had a quick look at the course shell. It looks clean. One thing I was not sure about: where will students find the lab safety video and quiz for Week 4? Is that under Labs or under Week 4 in the weekly modules?

I would put the safety video and quiz in both places: the Week 4 module for sequence, and a permanent link under Labs for quick access later. We can avoid confusion by using the same title and a note saying it is compulsory before any lab attendance.

I can configure the main menu as you suggested: Home, Weekly modules, Assessments, Labs, Support, Announcements. I will also add the safety video in both Week 4 and Labs as 492230 proposed. That should keep navigation straightforward and still highlight key items.

On the orientation module in T9, I think it should cover: 1) how the hybrid structure works (online versus on-site), 2) where to find weekly tasks and deadlines, 3) how assessments and feedback work (with a simple view of A2 and A6), and 4) where to get help. The low-stakes quiz should check that they know where to find things and what is compulsory.

Could we also include one or two questions in the orientation quiz about support options, like where to find the Support section and how to request adjustments? That will reinforce the inclusion plan from A3.
I like the idea of the quiz. Will we be able to see which students have not completed it easily, so we can remind them in class? I am not very familiar with the reporting options.

Yes, the VLE has a simple completion report for quizzes. As part of T8, I will set up a view that shows who has completed the orientation quiz and key early activities, and link that to the attendance and participation template in A8.

On attendance and participation (D7), I suggest we define a simple, repeatable process: 1) On-site sessions: record attendance directly in the VLE register within 24 hours. 2) Live online sessions: use the VLE attendance tool or meeting attendance report and copy into A8 weekly. 3) Asynchronous participation: track completion of key activities (orientation quiz, Week 2 quiz, one discussion post) using the A8 template. That should give us enough data without being too heavy.
That process sounds workable. Could we also agree that we will review the A8 data at the Week 2 and Week 4 check-ins from T11, so we can spot students who are not engaging early?

Yes, linking A8 to the check-ins in T11 will be really helpful. For colleagues who are less comfortable with the VLE, maybe we can include screenshots in A4 or a short how-to in the operations guide later, so the process is easy to follow.
I would appreciate screenshots or a short guide, yes. I sometimes forget where to click for the attendance register. If A4 or T12 can include that, it will save me time.

On D6, based on this discussion, I propose we confirm the VLE structure as: main menu with Home, Weekly modules, Assessments, Labs, Support, Announcements; weekly modules following A1; key items like the lab safety video and orientation module accessible both in the relevant week and in their dedicated sections. If everyone is comfortable with that, I will run a quick student-view test using A4 and mark T4 as ready for sign-off.
I am happy with that structure for D6. It is simple and matches what we have told students in other modules.
No objections from me. Once you have tested the student view, could you also check that the Support section clearly shows the inclusion summary from A3 and the contact routes?
I am ok with the structure. When you finish the student-view test, can you let us know if there is anything we should avoid changing later so we do not break the navigation?

To close D7, can we confirm that: 1) we will all use the A8 template weekly, 2) attendance will be recorded within 24 hours for on-site and live online sessions, and 3) we will track completion of the orientation quiz and at least two early online activities as part of participation? If yes, I will update A8 and T8 to reflect that and we can treat the method as agreed.
Yes, that works for me. Using the same template will make it easier to compare across groups.
Agreed. I will also use the A8 data when planning my check-ins, so it is not just based on who speaks up in class.
I am ok with that. Once we have the screenshots or short guide in T12, I will feel more confident using A8 every week.

Summarising: 1) We have agreed the VLE navigation and module structure as described in M70, and I will complete the student-view test using A4 and mark T4 ready. 2) The orientation module in T9 will follow A7, including questions on structure, assessments, and support, and we will track completion via T8. 3) For attendance and participation, we will use A8 weekly, record attendance within 24 hours, and track completion of the orientation quiz and early activities, as outlined in M66 and M74. With that, I think we can record D6 and D7 as agreed.

threads.thread_goal: Align on hybrid lab/practical procedures and team operations guide.

messages.text: Final piece to align: I have drafted hybrid lab and practical procedures in A5 for project_title: Hybrid First-Year Teaching Redesign with Virtual Learning Environments, linked to T6, and started a teaching team operations guide in T12 that pulls together A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, and A8. A5 covers lab safety, preparation, remote alternatives, and a supervision checklist. The operations guide currently includes: 1) weekly flow and key dates, 2) assessment and feedback norms from A6, 3) inclusion practices from A3, and 4) VLE and attendance processes. We need to review both and then sign off D8 on lab procedures and the consolidated guide.

I have read through A5. The safety and preparation parts are clear. For the remote alternative, where students join from home, I am not sure how much they are expected to do practically. Are they just watching a demo, or do they have a small task to do with household materials? I want to be sure I explain it correctly.

From a support perspective, I like that A5 includes guidance on pairing students so that those who cannot attend in person still feel involved. Maybe we can add a note about checking in with remote students at the start and end of each lab, so they do not get forgotten in the flow.

Looking at the operations guide draft in T12, I like the structure. Could we add a short section on communication norms from A6, including which channel to use for what and expected response times? That will help new colleagues joining mid-semester.

For the remote alternative in A5, I would keep it simple: students at home watch a live or recorded demo, complete an observation sheet, and answer a few application questions. If we suggest any household tasks, they should be optional and low-risk. We can clarify that in A5 so expectations are realistic.

Yes, I can expand the operations guide in T12 with a section on communication norms from A6 and T7: which channel to use for urgent issues, how we handle student emails, and our agreed response and feedback times. That will also help us stay aligned with what we promised students in the orientation module.

For the lab supervision checklist in A5, could we add one item about checking whether any students have disclosed specific needs that might affect lab participation, and making sure they have appropriate adjustments? That will tie A5 back to A3.

In the operations guide T12, I noticed we do not yet have a short calendar view of key weeks (assessments, labs, check-ins). Could we add a one-page overview so colleagues can see at a glance when the busy periods are?
I like that T12 includes screenshots of the VLE. Could we also have one example of a fully set-up weekly module, so I can copy the structure when I add extra materials?
I can help with the calendar view. I will pull dates from A1 and A2 and draft a simple timeline for T12, highlighting assessment deadlines, key labs, and the Week 2 and 4 check-ins from T11.

I will update A5 to clarify the remote alternative as 492230 suggested: observation plus application questions, with any household tasks clearly marked as optional and low-risk. I will also add the check-in with remote students at the start and end of each lab, and the checklist item about known support needs from A3.

On communication norms for T7 and A6, can we confirm that: 1) we use this Slack channel for day-to-day coordination, 2) email for formal student issues and anything that needs a record, and 3) the VLE announcements tool for whole-cohort messages? Response time for student messages within two working days, and for internal messages within one working day. If we agree, that can go into T7 and T12.
Those norms work for me. It will also help students if we are consistent about where they see announcements, so I am glad we are standardising that.
I am ok with that. Having it written in T7 and T12 will help me remember which channel to use.
Agreed. I will make sure the operations guide references A6 clearly so new colleagues can see the full detail if they need it.

To move toward D8, can we confirm two things: 1) A5, once updated, will be our standard for running hybrid labs, including safety, preparation, remote alternatives, and the supervision checklist. 2) The operations guide in T12, once we add the communication norms, calendar view, and example weekly module, will be our single reference for how we run this hybrid course as a team. Any objections to treating those as our agreed baselines?
No objections from me. Once the calendar and communication norms are in, I think T12 will be ready to share with any sessional staff as well.
I am happy with that. A5 and T12 together give a clear picture of what we are doing, and they reflect the inclusion and support decisions we made earlier.
I am ok with using A5 as the standard for labs. Having the checklist will help me feel more confident when supervising.
Same here. Once I finish the calendar view and you add the remaining pieces, I think we can treat T12 as our single source of truth for operations.

Great, thanks all. I will finalise A5 with the clarifications we discussed and complete T12 with the communication norms, calendar view, and example weekly module. Once that is done, I will share both with the programme coordinator for awareness. With that plan in place, I think we can record D8 as: lab procedures in A5 and the consolidated operations guide in T12 are approved as the standards for this hybrid course.
